description_full: Sendas Distribuidora S.A. engages in the retail and wholesale sale of food products, bazaar items, and other products in Brazil. The company offers grocery, food, perishable, beverage, wrapping, and hygiene products; and parking, air-conditioned, well-lit environments, and butcher services. It serves restaurants, pizzerias, snack bars, schools, small businesses, religious institutions, hospitals, hotels, grocery stores, neighborhood supermarkets, and individuals. The company sells its products through brick-and-mortar stores, as well as telesales. The company was founded in 1974 and is headquartered in Rio De Janeiro, Brazil.

financial_summary: Sendas Distribuidora S.A. is a mid-cap consumer defensive business with a $2.3B market cap on $13.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +21% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 255% against a 9% cost of capital — a 246-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 16% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $613M in free cash flow — roughly 4 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 6.41× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 1.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 1.1%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
